summary: Reserved-hours double-prorated due to half-hour timezone alignment causing unexpected mid-cycle charge
description: Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected mid-cycle charge for reserved capacity hours on the March billing snapshot. Impact: Finalized invoice shows an extra prorated reserved-hour line (0.5 hour duplicated) resulting in a $320 charge. Environment: Dedicated pool in ap-southeast-2; customer on dedicated monthly reserved plan. Steps to reproduce / observed behavior: 1) Customer scheduled reserved capacity 24/7 for March. 2) On 2026-03-05 23:30 local (ACST +09:30) an autoscaling event caused a short fallback to hosted for ~12 minutes while new nodes joined. 3) Billing shows two prorate adjustments covering the 23:00-00:00 hour: one standard prorate and a second 30-minute proration labeled as "smoothing-adjustment (timezone)". 4) Console estimate showed correct reserved discount; finalized invoice included additional prorated charge. Logs / evidence: Attached billing snapshot IDs and timestamps provided by customer; billing export row IDs: invoice_2026_03_line_4553, invoice_2026_03_line_4554. Customer provided console screenshots and CSV export. Customer request: Please explain why the 30-minute window was charged twice and reverse the erroneous charge if appropriate.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Customer (J. Patel, Aurelia Health): We were hit with a $320 surprise on our March invoice. The console estimate never showed this. We run in Adelaide (ACST +09:30) — looks like something happened late on Mar 5. Please advise.

2026-03-10 - Support (Marina Cortez): Thanks Jay. We received your attachments — opening an investigation with billing and infra to confirm proration logic for half-hour timezones. First response ETA by 2026-03-11.
2026-03-11 - Infra (Liam O'Neill): Noted. I've spun up INT-4021 to track autoscaler behavior during node join. Also pulling scheduler and allocation logs for 2026-03-05 23:00-00:30 local.

2026-03-12 - Billing (A. Reyes): Found two proration events: one canonical hourly proration and another smoothing adjustment triggered by a timezone-boundary alignment. Investigating whether half-hour zones are double-counted when smoothing window crosses non-zero-offset timezones.
2026-03-12 - Support (Marina Cortez): We will keep you updated; if confirmed we'll propose a one-off credit and follow-up with a billing fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Smoothing window algorithm assumes whole-hour timezone offsets; for zones with a non-zero minute offset (+09:30) the smoothing window boundary calculation created an overlapping proration slice (30m) that was applied in addition to the standard hourly prorate.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler fallback to hosted for ~12 minutes should have generated a single hosted-fallback prorate that gets normalized against reserved-hours; an edge-case rounding path emitted both a fallback prorate and a smoothing-adjustment prorate because of timestamp normalization at 00:00 UTC boundary.

Query run: billing.postback_rows where invoice_id = 'invoice_2026_03' and tenant = 'aurelia-health' returned two contiguous proration rows with identical usage_hash but different reason_codes (reserved_prorate, smoothing_timezone).

Scheduler logs: allocation change at 2026-03-05T14:42:00Z (23:12 local). Fallback duration 00:12:36. Autoscaler commit hash: a1b2c3d. Linked PR attempted to adjust smoothing window but was not backfilled for non-hour offsets.
Related codepaths: billing-service/proration.py : function compute_smoothing_windows likely assumes tz offset % 3600 == 0; missing branch for tz offsets with minute component.
resolution: Workaround: Applied a provisional invoice credit of $320 to Aurelia Health to offset the duplicated proration charge while engineering implements a fix. Next steps: 1) Billing QA to apply credit on customer ledger and confirm refund/credit note issued by 2026-03-13. 2) Engineering to patch proration algorithm to handle minute-offset timezones and add unit tests (PR scheduled: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/6789). 3) Post-deploy runbook update in Confluence to cover verification steps for half-hour and fifteen-minute timezones. 4) Follow-up summary to customer including root cause and timeline.
resolution_status: Credit applied pending formal refund note
notes_for_followup: Ensure billing export no longer contains duplicate proration rows for any tenant operating in non-whole-hour timezones (test with AU+09:30, IN+05:30).
Add an automated audit that checks for contiguous proration rows with overlapping timestamps and identical usage_hash to catch regressions in production.
Confirm with customer when credit appears on next account statement and provide finalized invoice PDF with corrected lines.
